title: Participles and relative clauses
content: Participles allow verbs to behave adjectivally, while relative constructions modify nouns with clauses. Egyptian has several strategies including participles, relative forms and relative pronoun-like elements depending on period and construction.

examples.english: hearing/listening one (illustrative root; exact morphology matters)

quiz.q: Can a verbal form modify a noun in Egyptian?

title: Numbers, dates and royal years
content: Egyptian numbers use repeated numerical signs and specialized notation. Dates can name regnal year, season, month and day. The calendar traditionally divides the civil year into three seasons—ꜣḫt, prt and šmw—each with four months, followed by epagomenal days.

quiz.q: How many named main seasons structure the Egyptian civil year?

title: Offering formulae and funerary texts
objectives: Analyze formulaic text rather than word-substitute
content: Funerary inscriptions are highly formulaic. A learner should identify titles, divine names, offerings, beneficiaries and grammatical links. Formulaic expressions are excellent reading practice because repeated patterns expose both spelling variation and stable syntax.

quiz.q: Why are offering formulae useful for learners?

title: Reading a real inscription: the analysis workflow
content: For a historical inscription: determine direction, identify signs and sign groups, produce a sign-level transliteration, separate phonetic complements from lexical consonants, identify determinatives, segment words, perform morphological and syntactic analysis, consult the lexicon, then translate. Preserve ambiguity instead of forcing certainty where the writing allows several readings.

examples.english: Anubis upon his mountain (classic instructional phrase)
